message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to not call my friend Tim by his preferred name Thor. Let me start by understanding the situation better. Tim and I have been friends for about 10 years, since our first year of high school. He's a bit hot-headed and has a short fuse, which makes being his friend a bit challenging at times. After high school, we started hanging out less because of college and work, but we still keep in touch occasionally. Both of us were born and raised in Canada, and Tim is of Icelandic descent. In Iceland, people often have both a Canadian birth name and an Icelandic name. Tim's Icelandic name is Thor, and while he didn't mind people calling him Tim in the past, he now prefers to be addressed as Thor. In fact, he's demanding that people call him Thor, and if they don't, he's cutting ties with them as friends. I've heard from my circle of friends that this is the case, and I haven't spoken to Tim about it yet, but we have a get-together planned in a few weeks, so I'll see him then. I plan to eventually start addressing him as Thor once I get used to it, but right now, I've been calling him Tim for 10 years, and I'm just not used to calling him Thor yet. The most likely thing to happen is that when I see him, I'll accidentally call him Tim and then correct myself to Thor. Knowing his short fuse, he won't like this. So, am I the asshole here? First, I need to consider why Tim wants to be called Thor now. Is it a cultural thing? In Iceland, people have both a birth name and an Icelandic name, so maybe Thor is more important to him culturally or personally. Maybe he feels that his Icelandic identity is more significant now, or perhaps he wants to be recognized by his Icelandic name rather than his Canadian birth name. On the other hand, I've known him as Tim for 10 years, and changing how I address him might feel unnatural at first. It's a significant change, and it's understandable that I'm not used to it yet. However, if Tim has made it clear that he prefers Thor, and he's even willing to cut ties with friends who don't respect his preference, then it's important for me to respect his wishes. But is it reasonable for Tim to demand that people change how they address him after 10 years? It seems a bit harsh, especially if he's been okay with being called Tim in the past. Maybe he's going through a phase where his identity is more important to him, or perhaps he's trying to assert his Icelandic heritage more strongly. I also need to think about how this affects our friendship. If I don't make an effort to call him Thor, even if it's difficult at first, it might send the message that I don't respect his wishes or that I don't value our friendship enough to make this change. On the other hand, if I do make the effort, even if I slip up occasionally, it shows that I care about his feelings and am willing to adapt for our relationship. Another angle to consider is the importance of names. Names are deeply personal, and being addressed by the name you prefer is a basic courtesy. If Tim has clearly communicated his preference, it's important to honor that. It's not just about the name itself but about respecting his identity and how he wants to be seen. However, I also need to think about the practicality of changing how I address him. Ten years is a long time, and habits are hard to break. It might take some time for me to get used to calling him Thor instead of Tim. I could make a conscious effort to practice his new name, perhaps by writing it down or thinking about it before our next meeting. This way, I can minimize the chances of accidentally calling him Tim. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can address him as Thor in public or in situations where his Icelandic identity is more relevant, but in private or in our one-on-one interactions, I can ease into the change more gradually. However, I need to be careful not to make it seem like I'm only addressing him as Thor when it's convenient or expected. Another consideration is how this might affect our friendship in the long term. If I don't respect his preference, it could lead to tension or even the end of our friendship, as he's indicated he's willing to cut ties with those who don't comply. On the other hand, if I do respect his preference, even if it's challenging, it could strengthen our relationship and show that I value him enough to make this change. I also need to reflect on whether I'm being reasonable in my hesitation. Is it really that difficult to change how I address someone I've known for a decade? Or am I just being stubborn or resistant to change? It's possible that I'm clinging to the past and not open to how Tim has evolved as a person. Being a good friend often means being adaptable and supportive of each other's growth and changes. In summary, while it's understandable that I'm not immediately comfortable calling Tim by his new preferred name, it's important to respect his wishes and make an effort to address him as Thor. This shows that I value our friendship and respect his identity. It might take some time and effort on my part, but it's worth it to maintain a healthy and respectful relationship.
